entry.title: Not Never More
entry.content:
In a reflection on the work, Jazz writes, “We inhabit our histories. We feel the pains of the past, we clang in its echoes, feel its residue caked up on our skin. History’s traumas have been perpetually erected in monuments, embedded in street names, stone walled in woodlands, hung, stacked, and plastered in architecture. Not Never More is my gut reaction and visual response to confronting such an architecture—the problematic 19th century French wallpaper Les Vues d’Amérique du Nord (The Views of North America), created in 1834 by Jean-Julien Deltil.”

Jazz worked with a team to produce the large, screenprinted Not Never More tapestries. The team included Anna McNeary, Yolizbeth Lozano, Sage Matsushima, Katie Gui, Simon Slowinski, Lyza Baum, and Joel Orloff. The work was originally installed at the Nightingale-Brown House, and was on view from April to September 2022.

Early on in planning the installation, Jazz approached me about collaborating on a publication to contextualize the work. The exhibition guide includes a portion of the tremendous amount of archival research that went into making Not Never More and contextualized the ways in which Jazz wove archival materials into the imagery of the tapestries. The exhibiton guide that was accompanied by a folio of RISO printed reproductions of the tapesties with a numbered key printed on sheets of transparent vellum.
entry.summary: Not Never More is a booklet and print folio accompanying an exhibition by Jazz Lee-Johnson. The installation consisted of screen printed tapestries displayed at Brown University. I designed, typeset and risograph printed the booklet and folio.

entry.title: Growing Guide
entry.content:
The Providence Seed Library was a public seed library offering free open-pollinated, heirloom, culturally relevant, and indigenous seeds founded and organized by Fatma Maswood. Seeds were available at branches of the Community Libraries of Providence.

In order to make the seed library accessible to less experienced growers and gardeners, Fatma taught a series of seed starting worksops. She asked me to help design and print this Gowing Guide to collect and share that curriculum more broadly.
entry.summary: The Providence Seed Library Growing Guide is a risograph printed book by Fatema Maswood. It was made with support from Community Libraries of Providence and Rhode Island Humanities. I designed and printed the booklets in collaboration with Fatema with illustrations by Carmen Ribaudo.

entry.title: Club Desire
entry.content:
Club Desire’s poems are set in the salt and smog-filled world of the upper Narragansett Bay, centering on Providence’s Allens Avenue and a fictionalized version of the strip club of the same name. When designing the book, I proposed makeing matchbooks for this fictionalized strip club, similar to ones I found in The Sexual Minorities Archive in Holyoke, MA.

Club Desire is a heterotopia where sites of extraction and waste are promiscously entangled with scenes of bodies in lustful embrace. Laura intentionally makes it difficult to delineate overlapping realities. For Laura, the strip club is a metonym for the excesses of capitalism and the orgiastic violence of settler-colonialism. It is a nuanced perspective where both sex work is work, and also work is often exploitation.
entry.summary: Club Desire is a collection of poems by Laura Lamb Brown-Lavoie. Each book is risograph printed, perfect bound, and comes with a book of screen printed matches. I designed, printed, bound, and distributed the books and fabricated the matchbooks with help from MJ Sanqui.
